stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google experienced its first negative cash flow quarter.
The primary driver for the negative cash flow is massive, skyrocketing AI spending.
Despite the cash flow dip, Google continues to report substantial quarterly revenue.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality model outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is its local-first architecture, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It integrates native support with Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, enhancing local AI capabilities on Apple hardware.
This is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy.
The core value proposition is connecting messaging workflows directly to local, private AI capabilities.

stories.title: TikTok’s protection of minors should not be opt-in, warns EU
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: The EU is scrutinizing TikTok's handling of minors' data and safety practices.
The European Commission is using the Digital Services Act (DSA) to issue preliminary findings against the platform.
The EU is urging TikTok to change the default settings for minors' public accounts to enhance protection.

stories.title: Facebook considers giving up and becoming TikTok
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Facebook is reportedly planning major platform changes to combat user migration to rivals like TikTok.
The proposed changes are described as a 'reimagined experience' and bear resemblance to TikTok's model.
The initiative, announced by Facebook head Tom Alison, is slated for testing later this year.

stories.title: Claude’s voice mode is now available for Opus and Sonnet
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Anthropic has expanded voice mode functionality to its more powerful Claude Opus and Sonnet models.
This update significantly increases the accessibility and capability of Anthropic's AI offerings.
Voice mode integration is being extended into major third-party applications like Gmail, Slack, and Canva.

stories.title: Forgot your Google password? Now you can log in with a selfie.
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is integrating selfie videos as a new method for account access and password recovery.
This biometric feature extends beyond security to include applications like AI Avatars.
The technology will also be utilized by Google for age verification purposes.

stories.title: Google hit with $1 billion in fines as EU braces for Trump battle
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Google has been fined $1 billion by the EU.
This marks Google as the third major tech company penalized under the Digital Markets Act (DMA).
The news is framed against the backdrop of potential future regulatory battles involving Donald Trump.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in handling complex 3D spatial reasoning tasks.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework designed to enhance 3D spatial awareness in VLMs.
The framework utilizes both implicit and explicit 3D geometries, incorporating Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) learned from RGB videos.

stories.title: GraphVid: Interactive Graph-Controllable Video Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: GraphVid addresses the challenge of precise multi-object interaction control in video generation.
It overcomes limitations of text prompts and trajectory-based inputs that struggle with scene complexity and occlusion.
The method introduces a graph-based mechanism for flexible and accurate multi-subject control in video synthesis.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: OpenForgeRL is a new open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end.
It addresses the difficulty of training agents that rely on complex, stateful inference harnesses (like Claude Code or Codex) using standard open infrastructure.
The framework enables agents to be trained across diverse environments while natively supporting multi-process harness inference.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of 2D-based Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in handling complex 3D spatial reasoning tasks.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework designed to enhance 3D spatial awareness in VLMs.
Achieves this enhancement by integrating both implicit and explicit 3D geometries, utilizing Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs).

stories.title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
stories.author: Tao Jin
bullet_points: Addresses the gap in deep logical reasoning capabilities of large audio-language models compared to text-based LLMs.
Introduces X$^3$-OPD, a cross-modal on-policy distillation framework.
The framework transfers advanced reasoning capabilities from a text teacher model to an audio-language student model.

stories.title: DONDO: Open w2v-BERT Speech-Recognition Base Models for African Languages
stories.author: Paul Azunre
bullet_points: Introduction of DONDO, a new family of open, permissively licensed ASR base models.
The models cover 27 language varieties across several African countries (e.g., Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana).
DONDO utilizes the w2v-BERT 2.0 self-supervised speech encoder, fine-tuned on religious texts.

stories.title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
stories.author: Alagappan Valliappan
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical performance bottleneck in speculative decoding when dealing with very long contexts (million-tokens).
The issue arises because standard Multi-Token-Prediction (MTP) draft heads incur a linear cost due to full attention over the growing KV cache.
The proposed 'Windowed-MTP' method aims to mitigate this 'Draft-KV Tax' to maintain efficiency at massive context lengths.

stories.title: India's first privately-developed rocket reaches orbit on dramatic debut launch
stories.author: sohkamyung
bullet_points: India achieved a significant milestone with its first privately-developed rocket reaching orbit.
This launch marks a notable advancement in the country's private space technology sector.
The event is considered a major development in the global landscape of private aerospace innovation.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This enhances the capabilities of local LLM execution by integrating advanced AI features.

stories.title: Patreon is laying off 20 percent of workers
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Patreon is conducting significant workforce reductions, laying off approximately 20% of its staff.
CEO Jack Conte addressed the layoffs, noting that AI has fundamentally transformed the tech industry.
The company explicitly stated the layoffs are not due to the belief that AI will replace humans.

stories.title: Robot snakes searched for Venezuela earthquake survivors in collapsed buildings
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: US robotics researchers deployed snakebots to search for survivors.
The deployment occurred in Venezuela following an earthquake.
The use of specialized robotics highlights real-world applications of search and rescue technology.

stories.title: Microsoft responds to LG monitors installing McAfee ads on Windows
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: LG monitors are reportedly installing McAfee advertising software on connected PCs.
The malicious installation occurs automatically via Windows Update when the monitors are connected.
Microsoft has responded to the issue, indicating awareness of the problem.

stories.title: AI Kill Switch Act would let Trump admin order shutdown of rogue AI systems
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: Proposed 'AI Kill Switch Act' grants authority to the Homeland Security chief.
The act would allow for the mandated shutdown of AI systems deemed 'rogue'.
This legislation represents a significant governmental attempt to regulate advanced AI safety.

stories.title: Sony's decision to ditch discs was practically inevitable, data shows
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Sony's move away from physical discs is presented as an almost certain industry trend.
The analysis is supported by Circana data indicating strong consumer preference in the US market.
The story focuses on shifting consumer behavior influencing major hardware/software decisions in gaming.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for time-series explanation.
Addresses a limitation in current methods by moving beyond mere 'sufficiency' to incorporate 'necessity'.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-weighted in model explanations, aligning with counterfactual reasoning.

stories.title: Beyond Sycophancy: Structured Resistance and Compliance in LLM Moral Reasoning
stories.author: Bernard Koch
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of simply reducing sycophancy in LLMs.
It proposes that socially calibrated LLMs must learn to distinguish between incorporating external perspectives and maintaining independent moral judgment.
The study identifies three structured dimensions governing how LLMs revise their judgments based on external input.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent visual reasoning capabilities, even on geometry problems.
The study highlights that different input modalities (text vs. diagram vs. combined) elicit different behaviors in VLMs.
The research suggests that these view-dependent inconsistencies point to complementary, yet separate, reasoning pathways within models.

stories.title: Expanding Flow Maps
stories.author: Pranam Chatterjee
bullet_points: Introduces Expanding Generative Flows (EFlows) to address limitations in existing flow-based generative models.
EFlows allow for generation across distributions of increasing dimensionality by augmenting the state with conditional noise.
The research aims to overcome constraints related to fixed dimensions or fixed sequence lengths in current generative models.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for explaining time-series classifiers.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods by incorporating 'necessity' alongside 'sufficiency' in explanations.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-weighted in model explanations, aligning with counterfactual reasoning.

stories.title: Graph Learning on Ensembles of Cyclic Peptides: An Investigation of Molecular Ensemble Modeling
stories.author: Maxim Secor
bullet_points: Introduces EnsembleEGNN, a new foundation model for molecular property prediction that accounts for conformational ensembles.
The model uses Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNN) to encode individual conformers, followed by a Set Attention Block for ensemble pooling.
It is pre-trained on CREMP, a dataset specifically focused on cyclic peptide ensembles, addressing a limitation in current single-conformation modeling.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent reasoning capabilities across different input modalities (text vs. visual diagrams).
The study, MIRROR, suggests that different views (text, diagram, combined) expose complementary, yet sometimes conflicting, reasoning paths in VLMs.
This highlights a key limitation in current multimodal AI, where performance isn't guaranteed across equivalent problem representations.

stories.title: MedGame: Storytelling Gamification Empowered by Large Language Models for Medical Education
stories.author: Qi Dou
bullet_points: Introduces MedGame, a framework that uses LLMs to transform static clinical cases into interactive, decision-centered storytelling games for medical education.
Addresses a limitation in current LLM medical tools, which often only provide localized interactions (e.g., Q&A) instead of full learning trajectories.
Employs a dual-engine design, featuring a Medical Narrative Designer, to structure and execute these complex clinical narratives.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: OpenForgeRL is a new open-source framework designed to train AI agents that rely on complex inference harnesses (like Claude Code/Codex).
The framework addresses a key limitation where existing open infrastructure struggles to natively support the stateful, multi-process nature of these advanced harnesses.
It enables end-to-end training of harness-based agents across diverse operational environments.

stories.title: GS-Agent: Creating 4D Physical Worlds With Generative Simulation
stories.author: Chuang Gan
bullet_points: The research introduces GS-Agent, a method to generate dynamic, physically realistic 4D worlds from natural language descriptions.
Current methods struggle with ensuring physical plausibility and controllability when generating complex 4D environments.
The work leverages recent advances in generative foundation models to automate the creation process, moving beyond manual computer graphics.

stories.title: What, Where, and How: Disentangling the Roles of Task, Language, and Model in Code Model Representations
stories.author: Piotr Wilam
bullet_points: The research investigates how different language models (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and DeepSeek-Coder-V1-6.7B) represent grammatical concepts in two different programming languages (Python and Rust).
It employs a 2x2 design to disentangle the influence of the specific task, the programming language, and the underlying language model on code representation.
The study aims to determine if independently trained code models converge on similar internal representations for the same concepts across different setups.

stories.title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks
stories.author: David Bann
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy constraint of using cloud-based LLMs for sensitive data preparation tasks.
Proposes using locally deployable, open-weight LLMs as a secure alternative for AI agent development.
Introduces an open-source framework to evaluate the performance of AI agents in this local, privacy-preserving environment.

stories.title: Sentry's Span Hierarchy Exposed a Silent Retry in My 5-Agent Pipeline. One Agent Took 22.6s, the Others Took 5.
stories.author: sarvar_04
bullet_points: The article details a performance bottleneck in a multi-agent pipeline using Sentry tracing.
A specific tool was identified as generating excessive output, causing significant latency variance across agents.
The solution involved implementing pagination and a token budget guard, resulting in substantial performance improvements.
